title: 2026 Bolivian Air Force Hercules C-130 crash

location.name: El Alto International Airport, Costanera Avenue

summary: A 49-year-old Lockheed C-130H Hercules carrying newly printed banknotes for the Central Bank of Bolivia landed at El Alto during heavy hailstorm. After landing, the aircraft veered off the runway, breached the airport perimeter fence, and collided with more than a dozen vehicles on Costanera Avenue, killing 24 people including 4 children. Technical report revealed the aircraft was at maximum capacity with pressure from delayed schedule, making safe landing at El Alto's 4,000 meter altitude physically impossible per aerodynamic laws.
probable_cause: Aircraft was carrying load at its maximum capacity at altitude of El Alto (over 4,000 meters), with heavy hailstorm during landing. The company delivering banknotes was behind schedule and under pressure, contributing to the overloading decision.

factors.evidence: a heavy hailstorm was reported at the time of the crash
aircraft was carrying load at its maximum capacity and the plane was physically impossible to land with that load at the altitude of El Alto (over 4,000 meters above sea level)
the company in charge of delivering the banknotes to the Central Bank of Bolivia was behind schedule, so it was under pressure
aircraft veered off the runway after landing, destroying the west side perimeter fence and entering Costanera Avenue

events.text: Heavy hailstorm reported during approach and landing at El Alto
After landing, the aircraft veered off the runway, destroying the west side perimeter fence
Aircraft entered Costanera Avenue where it hit more than a dozen vehicles, including private cars, public transport and cargo trucks
A total of 24 people died with 23 of the fatalities being people on the ground, of whom 4 were children

title: 2026 Colombian Air Force Lockheed C-130 crash
summary: A Colombian Air Force C-130H departed Caucayá Airport at 9:50 AM carrying 113 Army personnel, 2 police officers and 11 crew members on a troop transport mission. Shortly after takeoff, the aircraft began to lose altitude; one wing clipped a tree 1.5 km from the airport. The aircraft crashed into dense jungle near Puerto Leguízamo. The aircraft was destroyed by post-crash fire and ammunition detonated. Fifty-seven occupants survived with injuries but 69 were killed. The investigation was ongoing, examining three hypotheses: mechanical failure, pilot error, or excess weight.

factors.evidence: Investigators were focusing on whether excess weight contributed to the accident
United States and Colombian military officials had raised concerns about maintenance standards and availability of spare parts for Colombian aircraft
